newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares edge up 0.29 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares edge up 0.29 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares edged higher in thin and selective trade on Tuesday, despite profit-taking that followed the recent sharp gains, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed at a new all-time high of 88,335.02, up 255.16 points, or 0.29 percent from Monday's previous record of 88,079.86. But it was down from an early high of 88,799.
Trade volume plunged to 18.75 trillion lira ($185.6 million) from Monday's 26.24 trillion ($261.1 million).
"Selling began after an early rise, but switching of shares prevented a major fluctuation in the index," said Atilla Sozudogru from Soymen securities.
The index had gained 1.26 percent on Monday after a 5.38 percent surge last week when it pierced the stiff 85,000 barrier in a fourth attempt since late October.
Many brokers expect the market to drift sideways for awhile before attempting the next major target at 90,000.
